responseText: {"title":"When the Face Carries Signs","question":"What changes when a face holds letters, symbols, or objects instead of—or alongside—its features?","introduction":"These twenty-five works share a single territory: the human face as a surface where marks, symbols, and objects compete with portraiture. Some faces wear their signs lightly; others are nearly consumed by them. Moving from crossed eyes and barred mouths through gridded diagrams and split color fields, the exhibition asks what a face can still communicate once its features have been replaced, interrupted, or overwritten.","closing":"Each work leaves the question open differently. Whether a sign cancels a feature or simply joins it, something shifts in what the face can hold and what it can no longer say.","chapters":[{"title":"The X and the Eye","introduction":"Four faces where a single repeated mark—the X or cross—lands directly on the eyes, turning the gaze into a sign of blockage, alarm, or negation.","stops":[{"slot":"W008","whyHere":"Two large green irises each carry a bold red X; the mark dominates both eye zones and sets the exhibition's central question immediately.","transitionFromPrevious":null},{"slot":"W019","whyHere":"Flat black silhouette against pink; yellow X shapes inside rigid rectangular eye frames echo W008's crossed eyes but flatten them into pure graphic marks.","transitionFromPrevious":"Where W008's X marks sit inside spiraling organic irises, here they occupy hard-edged rectangles—the same sign, stripped of any biological surround."},{"slot":"W080","whyHere":"One eye burns red through a lattice of crossing lines; the other sits dim and closed. The X is now asymmetric, making the blockage feel uneven rather than absolute.","transitionFromPrevious":"W019 applied identical X marks to both eyes; W080 gives the crossing to only one socket, introducing imbalance where the previous face was symmetrically sealed."},{"slot":"W097","whyHere":"Dense crossed black lines fill both oval eye forms inside a loose white-line face; the marks read as sealed or blinded, the whole structure collapsing into dark ground.","transitionFromPrevious":"W080's asymmetric lattice eye still held a face in recognizable form; W097's crossed eyes dissolve into a muted brown field, the face barely holding together around them."}]},{"title":"Objects in Place of Features","introduction":"Works where a discrete object—a hand, a heart, glasses—occupies the position of a facial feature, displacing rather than decorating it.","stops":[{"slot":"W091","whyHere":"A pale hand pressed outward covers the entire eye zone; only teeth remain visible below, making concealment itself the dominant feature.","transitionFromPrevious":"W097's crossed marks sealed the eyes with line; W091 replaces the eye zone entirely with a physical object, making the absence of gaze literal and frontal."},{"slot":"W062","whyHere":"A dark-red heart with crossed yellow bars sits where eyes would be; the shape is affectionate in outline but damaged by the crossing, sitting above bared teeth.","transitionFromPrevious":"W091 used a hand to block the gaze; W062 substitutes a heart—a different kind of object, one that carries its own symbolic weight before the crossing marks complicate it."},{"slot":"W067","whyHere":"Rectangular glasses ride at two different heights across the face, one lens on the forehead, one near the eye—an object present but visibly displaced from its function.","transitionFromPrevious":"W062's heart was a substitution; W067's glasses are the correct object for the eye zone but sit askew, so the displacement is one of position rather than kind."},{"slot":"W071","whyHere":"Eyeglass frames form the one steady horizontal in an otherwise restless surface; they anchor the face while everything above and below breaks into competing marks.","transitionFromPrevious":"W067's glasses were slipping; W071's frames hold firm as the composition's single geometric anchor, making the object feel load-bearing rather than decorative."},{"slot":"W121","whyHere":"Flat-brimmed hat and oversized rectangular lenses compress the face into stacked zones; the hat and glasses together turn the head into a figure defined by its accessories.","transitionFromPrevious":"W071's glasses anchored a restless face; W121 adds a hat above them, so two objects now frame the face from top to bottom, leaving little room for features between."}]},{"title":"Marks That Compete With the Portrait","introduction":"Faces where geometric signs, scribbled lines, or color divisions actively contest the portrait for visual authority—neither fully winning.","stops":[{"slot":"W113","whyHere":"The face splits into warm red-brown and cool teal halves; looping pink crossed-oval eye marks and a dot row across the forehead divide the surface into competing systems.","transitionFromPrevious":"W121's objects sat on top of a coherent face; W113 divides the face itself into two color fields, so the split is structural rather than applied."},{"slot":"W115","whyHere":"Broad orange and cyan bands pass across the head, partially obscuring crossed yellow eye forms; portrait and horizontal color field compete across the same surface.","transitionFromPrevious":"W113's split ran vertically down the center; W115's bands cross horizontally, a different axis of interruption over a face that remains more naturalistically rendered."},{"slot":"W031","whyHere":"Stacked rectangular zones—hat, brow, eyes, mouth—each packed with crossing lines in lime, magenta, and red; the face becomes a column of pressurized compartments.","transitionFromPrevious":"W115's bands interrupted a recognizable head; W031 rebuilds the face entirely from stacked rectangular zones, so the compartmentalization is now the structure, not an overlay."},{"slot":"W095","whyHere":"Stripes, zigzag bands, spiral eyes, and a V-mouth stack in rows; the face is a flat grid of repeating marks rather than a modeled form.","transitionFromPrevious":"W031's zones were densely packed but still face-shaped; W095 flattens further into a striped grid where every zone carries the same visual weight."},{"slot":"W048","whyHere":"Two spiral-filled squares pull the eye inward while slashing straight lines cut through them at steep angles; the face is a site of competing directional energies.","transitionFromPrevious":"W095's marks ran in orderly rows; W048's slashing lines break that regularity, introducing diagonal force that cuts across the face's organizing structure."},{"slot":"W117","whyHere":"Saturated purple swallows the head's outline; yellow eye zones and a gridded jaw frame the face as something between a mask and a diagram, contained but restless.","transitionFromPrevious":"W048's energy was centrifugal, lines escaping outward; W117 pulls everything inward against a flat purple field, the face compressed rather than exploding."},{"slot":"W127","whyHere":"Hard-edged rectangles lock the eye zones while loose scattered strokes overflow the face boundary; a downward triangle anchors the lower half with green zigzag marks inside.","transitionFromPrevious":"W117's face was compressed by its ground; W127's face pushes back outward, its rigid frames surrounded by lines that refuse to stay inside the figure's edges."}]},{"title":"Letters, Numbers, and Diagrams","introduction":"Works where legible text, numerical signs, or diagrammatic layouts enter the face, making the image readable as both portrait and notation.","stops":[{"slot":"W061","whyHere":"Bubble-outlined letters NN, XYZ fill two framed rectangles in the upper left; a plus-in-circle and a row of oval loops complete a face-shaped schematic built from text and symbols.","transitionFromPrevious":"W127's face was built from geometric frames; W061 fills equivalent frames with actual letters and a plus sign, making the schematic explicitly linguistic."},{"slot":"W052","whyHere":"Three framed squares each hold a red X over a yellow circle—one more than a face typically carries—giving the structure a mechanical, serial quality.","transitionFromPrevious":"W061's letter blocks were unique; W052 repeats the same framed mark three times in a row, introducing seriality that pushes the image toward diagram rather than portrait."},{"slot":"W102","whyHere":"Identical lobed wheel eyes sit like dials on a teal ground; chained orange ovals, a bar of yellow blocks, and a dangling frame make the face read as something mounted or broadcast.","transitionFromPrevious":"W052's repeated X-circles were hand-drawn and rough; W102's lobed wheels and chained ovals feel more mechanical, the face assembled from components rather than drawn."},{"slot":"W085","whyHere":"Packed ladders, triangles, small heads, and a red heart-like form resist a single facial reading; the image oscillates between a possible face and a field of separate signs.","transitionFromPrevious":"W102's components were spatially organized around a face structure; W085 densifies the sign field until the face becomes one possible reading among many competing ones."}]},{"title":"The Face Nearly Gone","introduction":"Five works where the sign system has advanced so far that the face survives only as a residue—present in structure or placement but no longer dominant.","stops":[{"slot":"W013","whyHere":"A heavy mask sits against wavy orange stripes; red spirals, a bead row, and blunt white teeth give the face a ceremonial weight where ornament and structure are inseparable.","transitionFromPrevious":"W085's signs competed with a possible face; W013 presents a face that has become fully ceremonial, its features indistinguishable from the decorative system surrounding them."},{"slot":"W016","whyHere":"An orange-red arc, a bisecting vertical, an X, and a looping circle occupy the face zone; the composition resists settling into a fixed boundary or a readable portrait.","transitionFromPrevious":"W013's mask was heavy and frontal; W016 disperses the face into floating marks against a dark field, the portrait dissolving into its component signs."},{"slot":"W029","whyHere":"Three dripping columns dominate; small red marks at the edges are the only face-like accents in an image that reads primarily as abstract structure.","transitionFromPrevious":"W016 still held a face-shaped zone at center; W029 replaces it with columnar forms where facial features survive only as marginal red marks."},{"slot":"W111","whyHere":"A hooded purple form carries two white rectangular blocks—eyes and teeth—as flat mask segments; a yellow dot chain and spiky marks at one eye are the only signs of life in the dark mass.","transitionFromPrevious":"W029's face marks were marginal and small; W111 restores the face to center but as a mask of two flat white blocks, the portrait reduced to its minimum legible components."},{"slot":"W103","whyHere":"Circular glasses anchor a frontal face while scribbled lines radiate outward beyond the head's outline in all directions; the face holds the center as the sign system escapes around it.","transitionFromPrevious":"W111's face was absorbed into darkness; W103 reasserts a frontal presence, but the radiating lines suggest the face is actively losing its boundary to the marks surrounding it."}]}]}
